verdicts.trueWording: introductory boxed text section that runs more than a full page
verdicts.note: Live raw page (curl, browser UA, HTTP 200). Final section '1984 (c.) - Dungeonland & Temple of Elemental Evil'; the sentence names the Gygax/Mentzer Temple and puts the ~1,300-word figure in parentheses immediately after. Both limbs (word count, more than a page) supported.

verdicts.trueWording: room 404 is ironically a 20'×30' room with 1,200 words
verdicts.note: Same section and same sentence chain as 775; the page continues 'of content text' and adds room 417 at 1,400 words. Dimensions, word count and Temple attribution all on the page. Quote matched byte-for-byte including the × character.

verdicts.trueWording: start with some non-boxed info to the DM, and then
verdicts.note: Same final section: the page says Temple has a strong tendency to do this and gives the boxed description deep in the encounter text. The page's own hedge, that this is not universal, is consistent with the claim's 'tends to'.

verdicts.trueWording: not exactly in boxed text, but in specially quoted and indented
verdicts.note: Live raw page, HTTP 200. Section 'Other Curiosities', item 'Proto-Boxed Text'. The 1979 date limb is carried by the post's opening paragraph, which dates the Collector's Edition of Lost Tamoachan to TSR 1979. 'Initial descriptions for each area' matches the claim's 'initial area descriptions'.

verdicts.trueWording: The tactical format makes it difficult to generate a compelling adventure narrative
verdicts.note: Live raw page, HTTP 200. Opening sentence of the first quoted block. The '4e' limb is carried by Bridges' framing sentence directly above the block, which calls Cordell a main designer of 4th edition rejecting the current tactical format; post labels include '4th edition'.

verdicts.trueWording: adventures tend to be fairly Spartan affairs, because too little space
verdicts.note: Final paragraph of the same first quoted block; it continues with notes on exploration, lore and character story, so all three of the claim's listed omissions are on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: 1st Edition adventures I looked at included Tomb of Horrors
verdicts.note: Second quoted block, opening words; the block goes on to White Plume Mountain and Isle of Dread. The 'models of adventure format' limb is carried by Bridges' bridging sentence about going back to the classics for formatting examples.

verdicts.trueWording: compressed into single paragraphs with minimal effort spent on description
verdicts.note: Live raw page, HTTP 200. Section 'The Evolution of Dungeons & Dragons' Information Design', in the 4th Edition paragraph. The page hedges with 'often'; the claim drops that word but states a tendency, not a universal, so the limb stands.

verdicts.trueWording: it is a wall of text with a boxed description
verdicts.note: Same section, the paragraph comparing the author's copy of D&D5e's Candlekeep Mysteries to Temple of Elemental Evil. 'The blogger' is Brian C. Rideout, the post's bylined author.

verdicts.trueWording: rather than give a long box text, Hot Springs Island provides
verdicts.note: Section 'Point Form Description'; the sentence continues that the adjectives describe the area for the GM to use while improvising. The full title The Dark of Hot Springs Island appears in the adjacent section and image credit.

verdicts.trueWording: useful starting guidance on running an adventure that you wouldn’t find
verdicts.note: Live raw page, HTTP 200, Polygon excerpt bylined Jon Peterson. First paragraph of the excerpt under 'From the Unknown to the Borderlands'; the antecedent 'It' is In Search of the Unknown (B1) by Mike Carr, named in the preceding clause. Page continues 'in the D&D books available at the time', supporting the 'then-current' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: enlightening text about the art of dungeon mastering was effectively paraphrased
verdicts.note: Paragraph beginning 'It was then that Gygax apparently grasped'. The page says 'in Gygax's version'; that version is identified two sentences earlier as Keep on the Borderlands (B2), so the claim's naming of B2 is supported in context, not asserted beyond the page.

verdicts.trueWording: Modules only started to become a business for TSR in the summer
verdicts.note: First paragraph of the excerpt; the page completes the date as 'of 1978'. Claim's dating limb matches exactly.

verdicts.trueWording: points are made quickly and efficiently
verdicts.note: Live raw page, HTTP 200. Introduction, subsection 'The Base Rules', third point about the GAZ books; the same sentence notes casual, informal language and no overuse of purple prose. Subject is the Gazetteer series, matching the claim.

verdicts.trueWording: The first one clocks in at a mere 64 pages plus maps
verdicts.note: Same 'The Base Rules' subsection. 'The first one' is GAZ1: The Grand Duchy of Karameikos: the writeup proceeds in publication order and the very next heading is GAZ1 Karameikos; the GAZ1 conclusion later on the same page independently exclaims that it was only 64 pages.
